perspective:
From Sara Manuelito’s available perspective:

- Sara knows she is a speech-language pathologist working at a community health center. She knows Shirley Whiteplume as a long-time colleague and close friend.
- At the funeral of a mutual patient, Sara observed Shirley’s somber demeanor and suspected Shirley was deeply affected by the loss. Sara told Shirley she knew it was hard and that she had seen how much Shirley cared. Sara heard Shirley say it had been tough and that she kept wondering if more could have been done. Sara replied that they did everything they could and should remember the good care and moments of joy they brought; Shirley said it was hard to let go.
- During a coffee break at work, Sara brought up the patient’s treatment because she sensed Shirley felt burdened. Sara heard Shirley say she felt responsible and wondered whether pushing for a different approach might have given him a better chance. Sara said they made the best decisions with the information they had, and that the burden was too heavy to carry alone. Shirley said she appreciated that but it was hard to accept.
- During a quiet moment in their office, Sara observed Shirley continuing to be reserved and minimally expressive. Sara confronted her, saying it was okay to be open about her feelings. Shirley said she was not sure she could and did not want to seem unprofessional or weak. Sara said showing emotion does not make someone weak and is healthy among friends. Shirley said maybe Sara was right and she would try to be more open.
- Later, Sara felt her previous confrontation might have been too harsh, so she apologized to Shirley. Shirley said it had been a bit much but she knew Sara meant well and appreciated the apology. Sara said she was there for Shirley however needed. Shirley thanked her and said continuing to talk helped.
- After some time, Sara noticed Shirley seemed to be doing better and felt hopeful. Sara asked how Shirley was feeling. Shirley said she felt better thanks to their talks and Sara’s support. Sara suggested spending more time together outside work. Shirley agreed and said they should plan something for the weekend.

Sara has access only to what she directly observed, heard, did, or felt in these interactions; she does not have access to Shirley’s unspoken private thoughts beyond what Shirley expressed.
